nodes.statement:
ok
[Count vectors]
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, notation conventions.}
  A count vector of length \(n\) is a function \(c:[n]\to\mathbb N\).
  Its value \(c_i\) is the multiplicity of rank \(i\).
nodes.lean_source: def Counts (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℕ

nodes.statement:
ok
[Basis count vector]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, notation conventions.}
  For \(i\in[n]\), the vector \(e_i\) has value \(1\) at \(i\) and
  value \(0\) at every other rank.
nodes.lean_source:
def basis {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) : Counts n :=
  fun j ↦ if j = i then 1 else 0

nodes.statement:
ok
[Total tile count]
  
  
  
  The total number of tiles in \(c\) is
  \[
    |c|=\sum_{i\in[n]}c_i.
  \]
nodes.lean_source:
def total {n : ℕ} (c : Counts n) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i, c i

nodes.statement:
ok
[Removing a pair]
  
  
  
  If \(c_p\geq 2\), removing a pair at \(p\) means coordinatewise
  natural-number subtraction \(c-2e_p\).  The definition is available for
  every \(c,p\); the inequality is imposed by statements that use it.
nodes.lean_source:
def removePair {n : ℕ} (c : Counts n) (p : Fin n) : Counts n :=
  fun i ↦ c i - 2 * basis p i

nodes.statement:
ok
[Meldability]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, Definition \texttt{\#def-meldable}.}
  A count vector \(d\) of length \(m\) is meldable if there are
  nonnegative triplet counts \(t_i\) and run-start counts \(r_i\) such that
  \[
    d_i=3t_i+r_i+r_{i-1}+r_{i-2}
  \]
  for every \(i\in[m]\).  Run counts outside \(1,\ldots,m-2\) are
  interpreted as zero.  Thus no run may extend beyond the right endpoint.
nodes.lean_source:
def Meldable {m : ℕ} (d : Counts m) : Prop :=
  ∃ triplets : Counts m, ∃ runs : Fin (m - 2) → ℕ,
    ∀ i : Fin m,
      d i =
        3 * triplets i +
          ∑ j, if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0

nodes.statement:
ok
[Complete hand]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, Definition \texttt{\#def-complete}.}
  A count vector \(w\) is complete if some \(p\in[n]\) satisfies
  \(w_p\geq2\) and \(w-2e_p\) is meldable.
nodes.lean_source:
def Complete {n : ℕ} (w : Counts n) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : Fin n, 2 ≤ w p ∧ Meldable (removePair w p)

nodes.statement:
ok
[Live all-rank wait]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, Definition \texttt{\#def-live-wait}.}
  A count vector \(c\) is a live all-rank wait if:
  every coordinate is at most \(3\), its total is \(n+4\), and
  \(c+e_x\) is complete for every \(x\in[n]\).
nodes.lean_source:
def LiveWait {n : ℕ} (c : Counts n) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Fin n, c i ≤ 3) ∧
    total c = n + 4 ∧
      ∀ x : Fin n, Complete (fun i ↦ c i + basis x i)

nodes.statement:
ok
[The standard hand]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, finite-size reduction section.}
  The standard count vector \(G_n\) has multiplicity \(3\) at the two
  endpoints and multiplicity \(1\) at every internal rank.  The definition
  is made uniformly for all \(n\); the structural theorems only use
  \(n\geq6\).
nodes.lean_source:
def standard (n : ℕ) : Counts n :=
  fun i ↦ if i.val = 0 ∨ i.val + 1 = n then 3 else 1

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Rank sum]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, rank-sum invariant section.}
  For a count vector \(d\) of length \(m\), define
  \[
    \operatorname{rankSum}(d)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}i\,d_i.
  \]
nodes.lean_source:
def rankSum {n : ℕ} (d : Counts n) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * d i

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Scan state]
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, Definition \texttt{\#def-canonical-scan}.}
  A scan state is a pair \((a,b)\in\{0,1,2\}^2\).  The entries count
  runs started two and one positions earlier that must consume the current
  rank.
nodes.lean_source: def ScanState := Fin 3 × Fin 3

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[One scan step]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, Definition \texttt{\#def-canonical-scan}.}
  On input multiplicity \(z\), the step from \((a,b)\) fails when
  \(a+b>z\).  Otherwise put \(u=z-a-b\), let \(s\) be the least
  nonnegative residue of \(u\) modulo \(3\), and return \((b,s)\).
nodes.lean_source:
def scanStep (σ : ScanState) (z : ℕ) : Option ScanState :=
  if σ.1.val + σ.2.val ≤ z then
    some
      (σ.2,
        ⟨(z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) % 3, Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)⟩)
  else
    none

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Scanning a count vector]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, Definition \texttt{\#def-canonical-scan}.}
  Scan a count vector from left to right by repeated application of the
  one-step transition.  The result records either the first failure or the
  final state.  The operation may also be started from an arbitrary state,
  which is needed when a middle block is removed.

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Scan acceptance]
  
  
  
  A count vector is accepted when its scan starts at \((0,0)\), never
  fails, and finishes at \((0,0)\).
nodes.lean_source:
def ScanAccepts {n : ℕ} (d : Counts n) : Prop :=
  scan d = some (0, 0)

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Singleton finite sum by finite value]
  
  
  For a function on a finite interval, the sum that keeps only entries
  whose index has natural value \(i\) is the corresponding entry when
  \(i\) is in range, and is \(0\) otherwise.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  If \(i\) is in range, exactly one finite index has that natural value,
  so the sum has one nonzero term.  If \(i\) is out of range, no index can
  satisfy the equality, so every summand is zero.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma sum_if_fin_val_eq {m : ℕ} (i : ℕ) (f : Fin m → ℕ) :
    (∑ j : Fin m, if j.val = i then f j else 0) =
      if h : i < m then f ⟨i, h⟩ else 0 := by
  by_cases h : i < m
  · rw [dif_pos h]
    convert Fintype.sum_ite_eq' (⟨i, h⟩ : Fin m) f with j
    · constructor
      · intro hv
        ext
        simp [hv]
      · intro hj
        rw [hj]
  · rw [dif_neg h]
    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    intro j hj
    by_cases hv : j.val = i
    · exact (h (by simpa [hv] using j.isLt)).elim
    · simp [hv]

[Weight of one run in the rank sum]
  
  
  
  A run beginning at zero-based start \(j\) contributes the three
  one-based ranks \((j+1),(j+2),(j+3)\).  Hence its weighted contribution
  is \(3(j+2)\) times the run multiplicity.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Split the finite sum into the three possible coordinates of the run.
  The singleton-sum lemma evaluates those three terms, and their weights
  add to \((j+1)+(j+2)+(j+3)=3(j+2)\).
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma run_weight_sum {n : ℕ} (runs : Fin (n - 2) → ℕ)
    (j : Fin (n - 2)) :
    (∑ i : Fin n,
      (i.val + 1) * (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)) =
        3 * (j.val + 2) * runs j := by
  have hj0 : j.val < n := by omega
  have hj1 : j.val + 1 < n := by omega
  have hj2 : j.val + 2 < n := by omega
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n,
      (i.val + 1) * (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0))
        = ∑ i : Fin n,
            ((if i.val = j.val then (i.val + 1) * runs j else 0) +
             (if i.val = j.val + 1 then (i.val + 1) * runs j else 0) +
             (if i.val = j.val + 2 then (i.val + 1) * runs j else 0)) := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i hi
          by_cases h0 : i.val = j.val <;>
          by_cases h1 : i.val = j.val + 1 <;>
          by_cases h2 : i.val = j.val + 2 <;>
          simp [h0, h1, h2]; omega
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val = j.val then (i.val + 1) * runs j else 0) +
        (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val = j.val + 1 then (i.val + 1) * runs j else 0) +
        (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val = j.val + 2 then (i.val + 1) * runs j else 0) := by
          simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_assoc]
    _ = (j.val + 1) * runs j + (j.val + 2) * runs j +
        (j.val + 3) * runs j := by
          rw [sum_if_fin_val_eq j.val (fun i : Fin n => (i.val + 1) * runs j),
            sum_if_fin_val_eq (j.val + 1) (fun i : Fin n => (i.val + 1) * runs j),
            sum_if_fin_val_eq (j.val + 2) (fun i : Fin n => (i.val + 1) * runs j)]
          simp [hj0, hj1, hj2]
    _ = 3 * (j.val + 2) * runs j := by ring

ok
[Finite sum of zero congruence terms]
  
  
  If every term in a finite sum is congruent to \(0\) modulo \(3\), then
  the whole sum is congruent to \(0\) modulo \(3\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Induct over the finite set of summation indices.  The empty sum is zero,
  and adjoining one term preserves congruence to zero under addition.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma sum_modEq_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, Nat.ModEq 3 (f i) 0) :
    Nat.ModEq 3 (∑ i, f i) 0 := by
  classical
  exact Finset.induction_on (Finset.univ : Finset ι)
    (by rfl)
    (by
      intro a s has ih
      rw [Finset.sum_insert has]
      exact Nat.ModEq.add (h a) ih)

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Rank sum of a meldable vector]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, Lemma \texttt{\#lem-rank-sum}.}
  If \(d\) is meldable, then
  \(\operatorname{rankSum}(d)\equiv0\pmod3\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Choose triplet counts \(t_i\) and run counts \(r_i\) witnessing
  meldability.  A triplet at \(i\) contributes \(3i\) to the rank sum,
  while a run starting at \(i\) contributes
  \(i+(i+1)+(i+2)=3i+3\).  Every contribution is divisible by \(3\);
  summing them proves the congruence.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma meldable_rankSum_mod {n : ℕ} (d : Counts n) (hd : Meldable d) :
    Nat.ModEq 3 (rankSum d) 0 := by
  rcases hd with ⟨triplets, runs, hd⟩
  unfold rankSum
  have hrewrite :
      (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * d i) =
        (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * (3 * triplets i)) +
          (∑ j : Fin (n - 2), 3 * (j.val + 2) * runs j) := by
    calc
      (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * d i)
          = ∑ i : Fin n,
              (i.val + 1) *
                (3 * triplets i +
                  ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                    if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) := by
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro i hi
              rw [hd i]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * (3 * triplets i)) +
            ∑ i : Fin n,
              (i.val + 1) *
                (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                  if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) := by
              simp [Nat.mul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * (3 * triplets i)) +
            ∑ i : Fin n,
              ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                (i.val + 1) *
                  (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) := by
              simp [Finset.mul_sum]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * (3 * triplets i)) +
            ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
              ∑ i : Fin n,
                (i.val + 1) *
                  (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) := by
              rw [Finset.sum_comm]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * (3 * triplets i)) +
            ∑ j : Fin (n - 2), 3 * (j.val + 2) * runs j := by
              congr 1
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro j hj
              exact run_weight_sum runs j
  rw [hrewrite]
  have hTriplets : Nat.ModEq 3 (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * (3 * triplets i)) 0 := by
    apply sum_modEq_zero
    intro i
    apply Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd.mpr
    refine ⟨(i.val + 1) * triplets i, ?_⟩
    ring
  have hRuns : Nat.ModEq 3 (∑ j : Fin (n - 2), 3 * (j.val + 2) * runs j) 0 := by
    apply sum_modEq_zero
    intro j
    apply Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd.mpr
    refine ⟨(j.val + 2) * runs j, ?_⟩
    ring
  simpa using Nat.ModEq.add hTriplets hRuns

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Rank sum is additive]
  
  
  
  The rank sum of a pointwise sum of two count vectors equals the sum of
  their rank sums.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Expand the weighted finite sum and distribute multiplication over
  coordinatewise addition, then separate the finite sum into the two
  component sums.

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Rank sum of two basis tiles]
  
  
  
  Two copies of the basis vector at \(p\) have rank sum equal to twice the
  one-based rank of \(p\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  All coordinates except \(p\) vanish.  The remaining coordinate has
  multiplicity \(2\), so the weighted sum is \(2(p+1)\).
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma rankSum_two_basis {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n) :
    rankSum (fun i : Fin n => 2 * basis p i) = 2 * (p.val + 1) := by
  unfold rankSum basis
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * (2 * if i = p then 1 else 0))
        = ∑ i : Fin n, if i = p then 2 * (p.val + 1) else 0 := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i hi
          by_cases h : i = p
          · subst h
            simp [mul_comm]
          · simp [h]
    _ = 2 * (p.val + 1) := by
          rw [Fintype.sum_ite_eq']

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Rank sum of one basis tile]
  
  
  
  The basis vector at \(p\) has rank sum equal to the one-based rank of
  \(p\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  The basis vector has exactly one nonzero coordinate, at \(p\), with
  multiplicity \(1\).  The weighted sum is therefore \(p+1\).
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma rankSum_basis {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n) :
    rankSum (basis p) = p.val + 1 := by
  unfold rankSum basis
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * (if i = p then 1 else 0))
        = ∑ i : Fin n, if i = p then p.val + 1 else 0 := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i hi
          by_cases h : i = p <;> simp [h]
    _ = p.val + 1 := by
          rw [Fintype.sum_ite_eq']

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Adding one basis tile]
  
  
  
  Adding one tile at \(x\) increases the rank sum by the one-based rank
  of \(x\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Apply additivity of the rank sum to \(c+e_x\), then evaluate the rank
  sum of the basis vector.

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Rank sum after removing a pair]
  
  
  
  If \(w_p\geq2\), then the rank sum of \(w-2e_p\), plus twice the
  one-based rank of \(p\), is the rank sum of \(w\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Coordinatewise, adding back two basis tiles at \(p\) to the pair-removed
  vector recovers \(w\).  Additivity and the two-basis evaluation then
  give the displayed rank-sum identity.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma removePair_rankSum_add_pair {n : ℕ} (w : Counts n) (p : Fin n)
    (hp : 2 ≤ w p) :
    rankSum (removePair w p) + 2 * (p.val + 1) = rankSum w := by
  have hpoint : ∀ i : Fin n, removePair w p i + 2 * basis p i = w i := by
    intro i
    by_cases h : i = p
    · subst h
      simp [removePair, basis, Nat.sub_add_cancel hp]
    · simp [removePair, basis, h]
  calc
    rankSum (removePair w p) + 2 * (p.val + 1)
        = rankSum (removePair w p) + rankSum (fun i : Fin n => 2 * basis p i) := by
          rw [rankSum_two_basis]
    _ = rankSum (fun i : Fin n => removePair w p i + 2 * basis p i) := by
          rw [rankSum_add]
    _ = rankSum w := by
          congr 1
          funext i
          exact hpoint i

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Rank sum after choosing the pair]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, Lemma \texttt{\#lem-rank-sum}.}
  If \(c+e_x\) has a complete decomposition whose pair is at \(p\),
  then
  \[
    \operatorname{rankSum}(c)+x\equiv2p\pmod3.
  \]
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Removing the chosen pair gives the meldable vector
  \(d=c+e_x-2e_p\).  Its rank sum is divisible by \(3\) by
  Lemma~\ref{lem:meldable_rank_sum}.  Directly expanding the finite sum
  gives
  \(\operatorname{rankSum}(d)=\operatorname{rankSum}(c)+x-2p\);
  rearranging modulo \(3\) gives the claim.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma complete_rankSum_mod {n : ℕ} (c : Counts n) (x p : Fin n)
    (hp : 2 ≤ (fun i ↦ c i + basis x i) p)
    (hMeldable : Meldable (removePair (fun i ↦ c i + basis x i) p)) :
    Nat.ModEq 3 (rankSum c + (x.val + 1)) (2 * (p.val + 1)) := by
  let w : Counts n := fun i => c i + basis x i
  have hrem :
      rankSum (removePair w p) + 2 * (p.val + 1) = rankSum w :=
    removePair_rankSum_add_pair w p hp
  have hw : rankSum w = rankSum c + (x.val + 1) := by
    change rankSum (fun i => c i + basis x i) = rankSum c + (x.val + 1)
    exact rankSum_add_basis c x
  have hEq : rankSum (removePair w p) + 2 * (p.val + 1) =
      rankSum c + (x.val + 1) := by
    rw [hrem, hw]
  have hmod := meldable_rankSum_mod (removePair w p) hMeldable
  have h := Nat.ModEq.add hmod (Nat.ModEq.refl (2 * (p.val + 1)))
  rw [hEq] at h
  simpa using h

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Extended start lookup]
  
  
  
  Given normalized run-start counts, extend them to all natural indices by
  returning the indexed count in range and \(0\) out of range.
nodes.lean_source:
private def scanStartAt {n : ℕ} (starts : Counts n) (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if h : k < n then starts ⟨k, h⟩ else 0

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Cons for count vectors]
  
  
  
  A count vector can be obtained by placing a head value before a tail
  vector, with indices described by their natural values.
nodes.lean_source:
private def countsCons {n : ℕ} (head : ℕ) (tail : Counts n) : Counts (n + 1) :=
  fun i => if h : i.val = 0 then head else tail ⟨i.val - 1, by omega⟩

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[First incoming run component]
  
  
  
  At coordinate \(i\), the first incoming scan component is the initial
  state's first component at \(i=0\), the initial state's second component
  at \(i=1\), and otherwise the start count at \(i-2\).

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Second incoming run component]
  
  
  
  At coordinate \(i\), the second incoming scan component is the initial
  state's second component at \(i=0\), and otherwise the start count at
  \(i-1\).

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[First final scan component]
  
  
  
  The first component of the final scan state is the initial first
  component for the empty vector, the initial second component for length
  one, and the penultimate start count for longer vectors.
nodes.lean_source:
private def scanOut1 {n : ℕ} (σ : ScanState) (starts : Counts n) : ℕ :=
  match n with
  | 0 => σ.1.val
  | 1 => σ.2.val
  | k + 2 => starts ⟨k, by omega⟩

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Second final scan component]
  
  
  
  The second component of the final scan state is the initial second
  component for the empty vector, and the final start count for nonempty
  vectors.
nodes.lean_source:
private def scanOut2 {n : ℕ} (σ : ScanState) (starts : Counts n) : ℕ :=
  match n with
  | 0 => σ.2.val
  | k + 1 => starts ⟨k, by omega⟩

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Output shift after adding a head, first component]
  
  
  
  If a first scan step changes the initial state from \(\sigma\) to
  \(\sigma'\), then adding that head start before a tail preserves the
  computed final first component.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Check the possible lengths of the tail.  For length zero and one the
  claim is exactly the relation between \(\sigma\) and \(\sigma'\); for
  longer tails both sides select the same shifted start count.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma scanOut1_cons {n : ℕ} (σ σ' : ScanState) (starts : Counts n)
    (hσ' : σ'.1.val = σ.2.val) :
    scanOut1 σ (countsCons σ'.2.val starts : Counts (n + 1)) =
      scanOut1 σ' starts := by
  cases n with
  | zero =>
      simp [scanOut1, hσ']
  | succ n =>
      cases n <;> simp [scanOut1, countsCons]

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Output shift after adding a head, second component]
  
  
  
  Adding a head start before a tail preserves the computed final second
  component after updating the scan state.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  By cases on the tail length, the formula either reads the updated
  initial component or the same final shifted start count.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma scanOut2_cons {n : ℕ} (σ σ' : ScanState) (starts : Counts n) :
    scanOut2 σ (countsCons σ'.2.val starts : Counts (n + 1)) =
      scanOut2 σ' starts := by
  cases n <;> simp [scanOut2, countsCons]

nodes.chapter: Rank sums and the canonical scan
nodes.statement:
ok
[Output shift after removing a head, first component]
  
  
  
  Removing the head of the normalized starts shifts the first final output
  component exactly as a successful first scan step does.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Compare the formulas by the remaining length.  The boundary cases read
  the updated initial state, and the longer case reads the same shifted

private lemma scanPrev2_cons_succ {n : ℕ} (σ σ' : ScanState) (starts : Counts n)
    (hσ' : σ'.1.val = σ.2.val) (k : Fin n) :
    scanPrev2 σ (countsCons σ'.2.val starts) k.succ =
      scanPrev2 σ' starts k := by
  by_cases hk0 : k.val = 0
  · have hk : k = ⟨0, by omega⟩ := Fin.ext hk0
    rw [hk]
    simp [scanPrev2, hσ']
  · by_cases hk1 : k.val = 1
    · have hk : k = ⟨1, by omega⟩ := Fin.ext hk1
      rw [hk]
      simp [scanPrev2, scanStartAt, countsCons]
    · have hle : k.val ≤ n + 1 := by omega
      have hlt : k.val - 2 < n := by omega
      have hne : k.val - 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
      simp [scanPrev2, scanStartAt, countsCons, hk0, hk1, hle, hlt, hne]
      apply congrArg starts
      apply Fin.ext
      simp
      omega

[General scan decomposition]
  
  
  
  A decomposition from initial state \(\sigma\) to final state \(\tau\)
  consists of triplet counts and normalized start counts \(s_i<3\), such
  that \(\tau\) is the state predicted by the starts and every coordinate
  equals the two incoming starts, the new start, and three times a triplet
  count.
nodes.lean_source:
private def ScanDecomp {n : ℕ} (d : Counts n) (σ τ : ScanState) : Prop :=
  ∃ triplets : Counts n, ∃ starts : Counts n,
    (∀ i : Fin n, starts i < 3) ∧
      τ.1.val = scanOut1 σ starts ∧
      τ.2.val = scanOut2 σ starts ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n,
        d i = scanPrev2 σ starts i + scanPrev1 σ starts i + starts i + 3 * triplets i

[One scan step from a coordinate decomposition]
  
  
  
  If a coordinate has the form \(a+b+s+3t\), where \((a,b)\) is the
  incoming state and \(s<3\), then one scan step succeeds and outputs
  \((b,s)\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  The coordinate is at least \(a+b\), so the step cannot fail.  After
  subtracting the incoming components, the remainder is \(s+3t\), whose
  residue modulo \(3\) is \(s\).
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma scan_step_of_coord (σ : ScanState) (z s t : ℕ) (hs : s < 3)
    (hz : z = σ.1.val + σ.2.val + s + 3 * t) :
    scanStep σ z = some (σ.2, ⟨s, hs⟩) := by
  have hle : σ.1.val + σ.2.val ≤ z := by omega
  have hmod : (z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) % 3 = s := by omega
  simp [scanStep, hle, hmod]
  congr

[Coordinate decomposition from one scan step]
  
  
  
  A successful scan step from \(\sigma\) on input \(z\) to \(\tau\)
  provides a triplet count \(t\) such that
  \(z=\sigma_1+\sigma_2+\tau_2+3t\), and the first component of
  \(\tau\) is the second component of \(\sigma\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Success means \(z\) is at least the two incoming components.  Divide the
  residual by \(3\); the quotient is \(t\), and the remainder is exactly
  the new run-start component.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma coord_of_scan_step {σ τ : ScanState} {z : ℕ}
    (h : scanStep σ z = some τ) :
    ∃ t : ℕ,
      z = σ.1.val + σ.2.val + τ.2.val + 3 * t ∧ τ.1 = σ.2 := by
  unfold scanStep at h
  by_cases hle : σ.1.val + σ.2.val ≤ z
  · simp [hle] at h
    subst τ
    refine ⟨(z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) / 3, ?_, ?_⟩
    · change z = σ.1.val + σ.2.val +
        (z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) % 3 +
          3 * ((z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) / 3)
      calc
        z = σ.1.val + σ.2.val + (z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) := by omega
        _ = σ.1.val + σ.2.val +
            ((z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) % 3 +
              3 * ((z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) / 3)) := by
              rw [Nat.mod_add_div]
        _ = σ.1.val + σ.2.val + (z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) % 3 +
            3 * ((z - σ.1.val - σ.2.val) / 3) := by ring
    · rfl
  · simp [hle] at h

[Scan equals generalized decomposition]
  
  
  
  A scan of a vector from \(\sigma\) to \(\tau\) succeeds if and only if
  the vector admits the generalized coordinate decomposition from
  \(\sigma\) to \(\tau\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Induct on the vector length.  The empty case records that the initial
  and final states coincide.  For a nonempty vector, a successful first
  scan step gives the head triplet count and head start; the induction
  hypothesis handles the tail, and the shift lemmas translate tail
  coordinates and final outputs back to the original vector.  Conversely,
  the head coordinate decomposition forces the first scan step to succeed,
  and the tail shift lemmas provide the decomposition needed by the
  induction hypothesis.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma scan_iff_scanDecomp {n : ℕ} (d : Counts n) (σ τ : ScanState) :
    scan d σ = some τ ↔ ScanDecomp d σ τ := by
  induction n generalizing σ τ with
  | zero =>
      constructor
      · intro h
        simp [scan] at h
        subst τ
        unfold ScanDecomp
        refine ⟨(fun i : Fin 0 => nomatch i), (fun i : Fin 0 => nomatch i),
          ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro i
          exact nomatch i
        · rfl
        · rfl
        · intro i
          exact nomatch i
      · intro h
        rcases h with ⟨triplets, starts, hb, h1, h2, hc⟩
        simp [scan]
        rcases σ with ⟨a, b⟩
        rcases τ with ⟨c, e⟩
        simp [scanOut1, scanOut2] at h1 h2 ⊢
        apply Prod.ext
        · exact Fin.ext h1.symm
        · exact Fin.ext h2.symm
  | succ n ih =>
      constructor
      · intro h
        simp [scan, List.ofFn_succ] at h
        cases hstep : scanStep σ (d 0) with
        | none =>
            simp [hstep] at h
        | some σ' =>
            simp [hstep] at h
            rcases (ih (fun i : Fin n => d i.succ) σ' τ).mp h with
              ⟨tripTail, startTail, hboundTail, hout1, hout2, hcoordTail⟩
            rcases coord_of_scan_step hstep with ⟨t0, hcoord0, hσ'⟩
            have hσ'val : σ'.1.val = σ.2.val := by simp [hσ']
            refine ⟨countsCons t0 tripTail, countsCons σ'.2.val startTail, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
            · intro i
              cases i using Fin.cases with
              | zero =>
                  simp [countsCons]
              | succ k =>
                  simpa [countsCons] using hboundTail k
            · rwa [scanOut1_cons σ σ' startTail hσ'val]
            · rwa [scanOut2_cons σ σ' startTail]
            · intro i
              exact Fin.cases
                (by simpa [scanPrev1, scanPrev2, countsCons] using hcoord0)
                (fun k => by
                  rw [scanPrev2_cons_succ σ σ' startTail hσ'val k,
                    scanPrev1_cons_succ σ σ' startTail k]
                  simpa [countsCons] using hcoordTail k)
                i
      · intro h
        rcases h with ⟨triplets, starts, hbound, hout1, hout2, hcoord⟩
        simp [scan, List.ofFn_succ]
        let σ' : ScanState := (σ.2, ⟨starts 0, hbound 0⟩)
        have hstep : scanStep σ (d 0) = some σ' := by
          exact scan_step_of_coord σ (d 0) (starts 0) (triplets 0) (hbound 0) (by
            specialize hcoord 0
            simpa [σ', scanPrev1, scanPrev2] using hcoord)
        rw [hstep]
        apply (ih (fun i : Fin n => d i.succ) σ' τ).mpr
        refine ⟨fun i => triplets i.succ, fun i => starts i.succ, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro i
          exact hbound i.succ
        · dsimp [σ']
          rw [scanOut1_tail σ starts (hbound 0)]
          exact hout1
        · dsimp [σ']
          rw [scanOut2_tail σ starts (hbound 0)]
          exact hout2
        · intro i
          specialize hcoord i.succ
          dsimp [σ']
          rw [scanPrev2_tail σ starts (hbound 0) i,
            scanPrev1_tail σ starts (hbound 0) i]
          simpa using hcoord

[Run cover at one coordinate]
  
  
  
  For any coordinate \(i\), the finite sum over all run starts whose
  length-three window covers \(i\) has only the three possible
  contributors starting at \(i\), \(i-1\), and \(i-2\), with any
  out-of-range contributor interpreted as zero.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  A start \(j\) covers \(i\) precisely when \(j\leq i\leq j+2\), which is
  equivalent to \(j\in\{i,i-1,i-2\}\).  Split the sum into these singleton
  possibilities and use the out-of-range case of the singleton-sum lemma
  for nonexistent starts.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma run_cover_at {n : ℕ} (runs : Counts (n - 2)) (i : Fin n) :
    (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
      if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) =
        scanStartAt runs i.val +
          (if 0 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 1) else 0) +
            (if 1 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 2) else 0) := by
  calc
    (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
      if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
        = ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
            ((if j.val = i.val then runs j else 0) +
              (if 0 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 1 then runs j else 0) +
                (if 1 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 2 then runs j else 0)) := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro j hj
          have hiff :
              (j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2) ↔
                j.val = i.val ∨
                  (0 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 1) ∨
                    (1 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 2) := by
            omega
          by_cases hcover : j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2
          · rcases hiff.mp hcover with h0 | h1 | h2
            · have hnot1' : ¬(0 < i.val ∧ i.val = i.val - 1) := by omega
              have hnot2' : ¬(1 < i.val ∧ i.val = i.val - 2) := by omega
              simp [h0, hnot1', hnot2']
            · have hle : i.val - 1 ≤ i.val := by omega
              have hright : i.val ≤ i.val - 1 + 2 := by omega
              have hnot0' : i.val - 1 ≠ i.val := by omega
              have hnot2' : ¬(1 < i.val ∧ i.val - 1 = i.val - 2) := by omega
              simp [h1, hle, hright, hnot0', hnot2']
            · have hle : i.val - 2 ≤ i.val := by omega
              have hright : i.val ≤ i.val - 2 + 2 := by omega
              have hnot0' : i.val - 2 ≠ i.val := by omega
              have hnot1' : ¬(0 < i.val ∧ i.val - 2 = i.val - 1) := by omega
              simp [h2, hle, hright, hnot0', hnot1']
          · have hnot0 : j.val ≠ i.val := by
              intro h0
              exact hcover ((hiff.mpr (Or.inl h0)))
            have hnot1 : ¬(0 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 1) := by
              intro h1
              exact hcover ((hiff.mpr (Or.inr (Or.inl h1))))
            have hnot2 : ¬(1 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 2) := by
              intro h2
              exact hcover ((hiff.mpr (Or.inr (Or.inr h2))))
            simp [hcover, hnot0, hnot1, hnot2]
    _ = (∑ j : Fin (n - 2), if j.val = i.val then runs j else 0) +
          (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
            if 0 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 1 then runs j else 0) +
            (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
              if 1 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 2 then runs j else 0) := by
          simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_assoc]
    _ = scanStartAt runs i.val +
          (if 0 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 1) else 0) +
            (if 1 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 2) else 0) := by
          rw [sum_if_fin_val_eq i.val runs]
          change scanStartAt runs i.val +
              (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                if 0 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 1 then runs j else 0) +
                (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                  if 1 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 2 then runs j else 0) =
            scanStartAt runs i.val +
              (if 0 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 1) else 0) +
                (if 1 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 2) else 0)
          by_cases hi1 : 0 < i.val
          · have hsum1 :
                (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                  if 0 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 1 then runs j else 0) =
                    scanStartAt runs (i.val - 1) := by
                calc
                  (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                    if 0 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 1 then runs j else 0)
                      = ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                          if j.val = i.val - 1 then runs j else 0 := by
                            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
                            intro j hj
                            simp [hi1]
                  _ = scanStartAt runs (i.val - 1) := by
                        rw [sum_if_fin_val_eq (i.val - 1) runs]
                        rfl
            rw [if_pos hi1, hsum1]
            by_cases hi2 : 1 < i.val
            · have hsum2 :
                  (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                    if 1 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 2 then runs j else 0) =
                      scanStartAt runs (i.val - 2) := by
                  calc
                    (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                      if 1 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 2 then runs j else 0)
                        = ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                            if j.val = i.val - 2 then runs j else 0 := by
                              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
                              intro j hj
                              simp [hi2]
                    _ = scanStartAt runs (i.val - 2) := by
                          rw [sum_if_fin_val_eq (i.val - 2) runs]
                          rfl
              rw [if_pos hi2, hsum2]
            · rw [if_neg hi2]
              have hzero :
                  (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                    if 1 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 2 then runs j else 0) = 0 := by
                apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
                intro j hj
                simp [hi2]
              rw [hzero]
          · rw [if_neg hi1]
            have hnot2 : ¬1 < i.val := by omega
            have hzero1 :
                (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                  if 0 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 1 then runs j else 0) = 0 := by
              apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
              intro j hj
              simp [hi1]
            have hzero2 :
                (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                  if 1 < i.val ∧ j.val = i.val - 2 then runs j else 0) = 0 := by
              apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
              intro j hj
              simp [hnot2]
            rw [if_neg hnot2, hzero1, hzero2]

nodes.statement:
ok
[Canonical scan characterizes meldability]
  
  
  
  
  
  \textit{Source: half-formal.qmd, Lemma \texttt{\#lem-recurrence}.}
  A count vector is meldable if and only if its canonical scan is
  accepted.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  First suppose a meld decomposition is given.  At each run start, replace
  groups of three identical runs by one triplet at each of their three
  ranks.  This preserves the count vector and leaves every run count in
  \(\{0,1,2\}\).  Inducting from left to right, the two incoming run counts
  are exactly the scan state.  After subtracting them, the residual is
  \(3t_i+r_i\), so its residue modulo \(3\) is the normalized run count
  \(r_i\).  The scan therefore follows these run counts, never fails, and
  ends at zero because no run starts in either of the final two positions.

  Conversely, suppose the scan accepts.  At coordinate \(i\), let \(s_i\)
  be the new second state component and let
  \(u_i=d_i-s_{i-2}-s_{i-1}\).  Nonfailure gives \(u_i\geq0\), and the
  transition rule makes \(u_i-s_i\) a nonnegative multiple of \(3\).
  Set \(t_i=(u_i-s_i)/3\).  Then
  \[
    d_i=3t_i+s_i+s_{i-1}+s_{i-2}.
  \]
  Acceptance says the final two run counts are zero, so these \(t_i,s_i\)
  form a legal meld decomposition.

  In the finite-vector implementation, package the recurrence as the
  generalized decomposition from Lemma~\ref{lem:scan_iff_scan_decomp}.  In
  the forward direction, replace every original run count \(r_j\) by its
  residue \(r_j\bmod 3\) plus \(3\lfloor r_j/3\rfloor\); the quotient
  contributions are absorbed into the triplet counts.  In the reverse
  direction, Lemma~\ref{lem:run_cover_at} rewrites the original meldability
  cover sum at coordinate \(i\) as exactly the incoming starts from
  \(i-2\), \(i-1\), and \(i\).  The final two output equalities ensure
  that no run starts in the two invalid right-end positions.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem meldable_iff_scanAccepts {n : ℕ} (d : Counts n) :
    Meldable d ↔ ScanAccepts d := by
  constructor
  · intro hd
    rcases hd with ⟨triplets, runs, hcoord⟩
    let starts : Counts n :=
      fun i => if h : i.val < n - 2 then runs ⟨i.val, h⟩ % 3 else 0
    let triplets' : Counts n :=
      fun i =>
        triplets i +
          ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
            if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j / 3 else 0
    have hdec : ScanDecomp d (0, 0) (0, 0) := by
      refine ⟨triplets', starts, ?hbound, ?hout1, ?hout2, ?hcoord'⟩
      · intro i
        dsimp [starts]
        split_ifs <;> omega
      · dsimp [starts, scanOut1]

        split <;> simp
      · dsimp [starts, scanOut2]

        split <;> simp
      · intro i
        have hi := hcoord i

        have hstartAt : ∀ k : ℕ, scanStartAt starts k = scanStartAt runs k % 3 := by
          intro k
          by_cases hk : k < n - 2
          · have hkn : k < n := by omega
            simp [scanStartAt, starts, hk, hkn]
          · simp [scanStartAt, starts, hk]
        have hquotAt : ∀ k : ℕ,
            scanStartAt (fun j : Fin (n - 2) => runs j / 3) k = scanStartAt runs k / 3 := by
          intro k
          by_cases hk : k < n - 2
          · simp [scanStartAt, hk]
          · simp [scanStartAt, hk]
        have hprev2 : scanPrev2 (0, 0) starts i =
            (if 1 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 2) % 3 else 0) := by
          dsimp [scanPrev2]
          by_cases hi0 : i.val = 0
          · simp [hi0]
          · by_cases hi1eq : i.val = 1
            · simp [hi1eq]
            · have hi2 : 1 < i.val := by omega
              simp [hi0, hi1eq, hi2, hstartAt]
        have hprev1 : scanPrev1 (0, 0) starts i =
            (if 0 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 1) % 3 else 0) := by
          dsimp [scanPrev1]
          by_cases hi0 : i.val = 0
          · simp [hi0]
          · have hi1 : 0 < i.val := by omega
            simp [hi0, hi1, hstartAt]
        have hstarti : starts i = scanStartAt runs i.val % 3 := by
          dsimp [starts, scanStartAt]
          by_cases hk : i.val < n - 2
          · simp [hk]
          · simp [hk]
        have hcover := run_cover_at runs i
        have hcoverQ := run_cover_at (fun j : Fin (n - 2) => runs j / 3) i
        have hdecomp0 : scanStartAt runs i.val =
            scanStartAt runs i.val % 3 + 3 * (scanStartAt runs i.val / 3) := by
          rw [Nat.mod_add_div]
        have hdecomp1 : (if 0 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 1) else 0) =
            (if 0 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 1) % 3 else 0) +
              3 * (if 0 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 1) / 3 else 0) := by
          by_cases hi1 : 0 < i.val <;> simp [hi1, Nat.mod_add_div]
        have hdecomp2 : (if 1 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 2) else 0) =
            (if 1 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 2) % 3 else 0) +
              3 * (if 1 < i.val then scanStartAt runs (i.val - 2) / 3 else 0) := by
          by_cases hi2 : 1 < i.val <;> simp [hi2, Nat.mod_add_div]
        rw [hi, hcover]
        dsimp [triplets']
        rw [hcoverQ]
        rw [hprev2, hprev1, hstarti]
        repeat rw [hquotAt]
        omega
    exact (scan_iff_scanDecomp d (0, 0) (0, 0)).mpr hdec
  · intro hscan
    rcases (scan_iff_scanDecomp d (0, 0) (0, 0)).mp hscan with
      ⟨triplets, starts, hbound, hout1, hout2, hcoord⟩
    refine ⟨triplets, (fun j : Fin (n - 2) => starts ⟨j.val, by omega⟩), ?_⟩
    intro i
    have hi := hcoord i

    let runs' : Counts (n - 2) := fun j : Fin (n - 2) => starts ⟨j.val, by omega⟩
    have hout1_zero : ∀ k (hk : k + 2 = n), starts ⟨k, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
      intro k hk
      subst n
      simpa [scanOut1] using hout1.symm
    have hout2_zero : ∀ k (hk : k + 1 = n), starts ⟨k, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
      intro k hk
      subst n
      simpa [scanOut2] using hout2.symm
    have hcurrent : starts i = scanStartAt runs' i.val := by
      by_cases hk : i.val < n - 2
      · dsimp [runs']
        simp [scanStartAt, hk]
      · have hrunzero : scanStartAt runs' i.val = 0 := by
          simp [scanStartAt, hk]
        rw [hrunzero]
        have hcase : i.val + 2 = n ∨ i.val + 1 = n := by omega
        rcases hcase with hN | hN
        · simpa using hout1_zero i.val hN
        · simpa using hout2_zero i.val hN
    have hprev1 : scanPrev1 (0, 0) starts i =
        (if 0 < i.val then scanStartAt runs' (i.val - 1) else 0) := by
      dsimp [scanPrev1]
      by_cases hi0 : i.val = 0
      · simp [hi0]
      · have hi_pos : 0 < i.val := by omega
        have hlookup : scanStartAt starts (i.val - 1) = scanStartAt runs' (i.val - 1) := by
          by_cases hk : i.val - 1 < n - 2
          · have hkn : i.val - 1 < n := by omega
            dsimp [runs']
            simp [scanStartAt, hk, hkn]
          · have hN : i.val - 1 + 2 = n := by omega
            have hkn : i.val - 1 < n := by omega
            have hleft : scanStartAt starts (i.val - 1) = 0 := by
              simpa [scanStartAt, hkn] using hout1_zero (i.val - 1) hN
            have hright : scanStartAt runs' (i.val - 1) = 0 := by
              simp [scanStartAt, hk]
            rw [hleft, hright]
        simp [hi0, hi_pos, hlookup]
    have hprev2 : scanPrev2 (0, 0) starts i =
        (if 1 < i.val then scanStartAt runs' (i.val - 2) else 0) := by
      dsimp [scanPrev2]
      by_cases hi0 : i.val = 0
      · simp [hi0]
      · by_cases hi1eq : i.val = 1
        · simp [hi1eq]
        · have hi2 : 1 < i.val := by omega
          have hk : i.val - 2 < n - 2 := by omega
          have hkn : i.val - 2 < n := by omega
          dsimp [runs']
          simp [hi0, hi1eq, hi2, scanStartAt, hk, hkn]
    have hcover := run_cover_at runs' i
    rw [hi, hcover]
    rw [hprev2, hprev1, hcurrent]
    omega

lemma scanStep_one :
    scanStep (0, 0) 1 = some (0, 1) ∧
      scanStep (0, 1) 1 = some (1, 0) ∧
      scanStep (1, 0) 1 = some (0, 0) ∧

  · rfl
  constructor
  · rfl
  constructor
  · rfl
  · intro σ
    constructor
    · intro h
      rcases σ with ⟨a, b⟩
      fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> simp [scanStep] at h ⊢

[A zero total has zero terms]

  summand is \(0\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Each summand is bounded above by the whole finite sum.  If the whole
  sum is \(0\), antisymmetry in \(\mathbb N\) forces the chosen summand
  to be \(0\).
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma eq_zero_of_sum_eq_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {f : ι → ℕ} (hsum : (∑ i, f i) = 0) (i : ι) :
    f i = 0 := by
  have hle : f i ≤ ∑ j, f j := by
    exact Finset.single_le_sum (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Finset.mem_univ i)
  omega

[Unweighted contribution of one run]
  
  
  
  A run beginning at zero-based start \(j\) contributes exactly three
  tiles to the unweighted total, counted with its multiplicity.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Split the finite sum into the three coordinates \(j,j+1,j+2\).  The
  singleton finite-sum lemma evaluates those three terms and all other
  coordinates contribute \(0\).
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma run_count_sum {n : ℕ} (runs : Fin (n - 2) → ℕ)
    (j : Fin (n - 2)) :
    (∑ i : Fin n,
      if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) =
        3 * runs j := by
  have hj0 : j.val < n := by omega
  have hj1 : j.val + 1 < n := by omega
  have hj2 : j.val + 2 < n := by omega
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n,
      if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
        = ∑ i : Fin n,
            ((if i.val = j.val then runs j else 0) +
             (if i.val = j.val + 1 then runs j else 0) +
             (if i.val = j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)) := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i hi
          by_cases h0 : i.val = j.val <;>
          by_cases h1 : i.val = j.val + 1 <;>
          by_cases h2 : i.val = j.val + 2 <;>
          simp [h0, h1, h2]; omega
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val = j.val then runs j else 0) +
        (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val = j.val + 1 then runs j else 0) +
        (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val = j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) := by
          simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_assoc]
    _ = runs j + runs j + runs j := by
          rw [sum_if_fin_val_eq j.val (fun _ : Fin n => runs j),
            sum_if_fin_val_eq (j.val + 1) (fun _ : Fin n => runs j),
            sum_if_fin_val_eq (j.val + 2) (fun _ : Fin n => runs j)]
          simp [hj0, hj1, hj2]
    _ = 3 * runs j := by ring

[Filtered totals are additive]
  
  
  For any predicate \(P\) on the finite coordinate set, the sum of
  \(a_i+b_i\) over the coordinates satisfying \(P\) is the sum over
  \(a_i\) plus the sum over \(b_i\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Distribute addition inside each selected summand, then split the finite
  sum into the two component sums.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma filteredTotal_add {n : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P]
    (a b : Counts n) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then a i + b i else 0) =
      (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then a i else 0) +
        (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then b i else 0) := by
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then a i + b i else 0)
        = ∑ i : Fin n, ((if P i then a i else 0) + (if P i then b i else 0)) := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i hi
          by_cases hP : P i <;> simp [hP]
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then a i else 0) +
          (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then b i else 0) := by
          simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib]

private lemma filteredRank_add {n : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P]

              (if P i then (i.val + 1) * b i else 0)) := by

[Filtered total of a basis vector]
  
  
  
  A multiple of the basis vector at \(x\) contributes \(m\) to a filtered
  total exactly when \(x\) satisfies the filter, and contributes \(0\)
  otherwise.
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  If \(x\) satisfies the filter, the finite sum has the single nonzero
  coordinate \(x\).  If it does not, every selected coordinate has zero
  basis value.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma filteredTotal_basis {n : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P]
    (x : Fin n) (m : ℕ) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then m * basis x i else 0) =
      if P x then m else 0 := by
  by_cases hx : P x
  · calc
      (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then m * basis x i else 0)
          = ∑ i : Fin n, if i = x then m else 0 := by
            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
            intro i hi
            by_cases hix : i = x
            · subst i
              simp [basis, hx]
            · simp [basis, hix]
      _ = m := by rw [Fintype.sum_ite_eq']
      _ = if P x then m else 0 := by simp [hx]
  · have hzero :
        (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then m * basis x i else 0) = 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro i hi
      by_cases hP : P i
      · have hix : i ≠ x := by
          intro h
          subst i
          exact hx hP
        simp [hP, basis, hix]
      · simp [hP]
    rw [hzero]
    simp [hx]

private lemma filteredRank_basis {n : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P]
    (x : Fin n) (m : ℕ) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then (i.val + 1) * (m * basis x i) else 0) =
      if P x then (x.val + 1) * m else 0 := by
  by_cases hx : P x
  · calc
      (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then (i.val + 1) * (m * basis x i) else 0)
          = ∑ i : Fin n, if i = x then (x.val + 1) * m else 0 := by
            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
            intro i hi
            by_cases hix : i = x
            · subst i
              simp [basis, hx]
            · simp [basis, hix]
      _ = (x.val + 1) * m := by rw [Fintype.sum_ite_eq']
      _ = if P x then (x.val + 1) * m else 0 := by simp [hx]
  · have hzero :
        (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then (i.val + 1) * (m * basis x i) else 0) = 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro i hi
      by_cases hP : P i
      · have hix : i ≠ x := by
          intro h
          subst i
          exact hx hP
        simp [hP, basis, hix]
      · simp [hP]

    simp [hx]

[Filtered total after a draw]
  
  
  
  Adding one tile at \(x\) increases a filtered total by \(1\) if \(x\)
  satisfies the filter, and by \(0\) otherwise.

\leanok
  Apply filtered additivity to split off the basis vector, then evaluate
  that filtered basis contribution.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma filteredTotal_add_basis {n : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P]
    (c : Counts n) (x : Fin n) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then c i + basis x i else 0) =
      (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then c i else 0) + if P x then 1 else 0 := by
  rw [filteredTotal_add P c (basis x)]
  have hb := filteredTotal_basis P x 1
  simpa using congrArg (fun t => (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then c i else 0) + t) hb

private lemma filteredRank_add_basis {n : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P]

[Filtered total after removing a pair]
  
  
  
  If \(w_p\ge2\), then the filtered total of \(w-2e_p\), plus the two
  removed tiles when \(p\) is selected by the filter, equals the filtered
  total of \(w\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Coordinatewise, adding two basis tiles at \(p\) back to \(w-2e_p\)
  recovers \(w\).  Apply filtered additivity and the filtered basis
  evaluation.
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma filteredTotal_removePair_add_pair {n : ℕ}
    (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P] (w : Counts n) (p : Fin n)
    (hp : 2 ≤ w p) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then removePair w p i else 0) +
        (if P p then 2 else 0) =
      (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then w i else 0) := by
  have hpoint : ∀ i : Fin n, removePair w p i + 2 * basis p i = w i := by
    intro i
    by_cases h : i = p
    · subst i
      simp [removePair, basis, Nat.sub_add_cancel hp]
    · simp [removePair, basis, h]
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then removePair w p i else 0) + (if P p then 2 else 0)
        = (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then removePair w p i else 0) +
            (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then 2 * basis p i else 0) := by
            rw [filteredTotal_basis P p 2]
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then removePair w p i + 2 * basis p i else 0) := by
          rw [filteredTotal_add]
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then w i else 0) := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i hi
          rw [hpoint i]

private lemma filteredRank_removePair_add_pair {n : ℕ}
    (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P] (w : Counts n) (p : Fin n)
    (hp : 2 ≤ w p) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then (i.val + 1) * removePair w p i else 0) +
        (if P p then (p.val + 1) * 2 else 0) =
      (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then (i.val + 1) * w i else 0) := by
  have hpoint : ∀ i : Fin n, removePair w p i + 2 * basis p i = w i := by
    intro i
    by_cases h : i = p
    · subst i
      simp [removePair, basis, Nat.sub_add_cancel hp]
    · simp [removePair, basis, h]
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then (i.val + 1) * removePair w p i else 0) +
        (if P p then (p.val + 1) * 2 else 0)
        = (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then (i.val + 1) * removePair w p i else 0) +
            (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then (i.val + 1) * (2 * basis p i) else 0) := by
            rw [filteredRank_basis P p 2]
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n,
          if P i then (i.val + 1) * (removePair w p i + 2 * basis p i) else 0) := by
          rw [filteredRank_add]
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if P i then (i.val + 1) * w i else 0) := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i hi
          rw [hpoint i]

[Total split at a cut]
  
  
  
  The total count is the sum of the counts strictly left of \(k\), at
  \(k\), and strictly right of \(k\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Partition every coordinate into the trichotomy \(i<k\), \(i=k\), or
  \(k<i\).  The middle singleton sum evaluates to \(c_k\).
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma total_split_at {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n) (c : Counts n) :
    total c = leftTotal k c + c k + rightTotal k c := by
  unfold total leftTotal rightTotal
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n, c i)
        = ∑ i : Fin n,
            ((if i.val < k.val then c i else 0) +
              (if i.val = k.val then c i else 0) +
              (if k.val < i.val then c i else 0)) := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i hi
          by_cases hlt : i.val < k.val
          · have hne : i.val ≠ k.val := by omega
            have hnotgt : ¬ k.val < i.val := by omega
            simp [hlt, hne, hnotgt]
          · by_cases heq : i.val = k.val
            · simp [heq]
            · have hgt : k.val < i.val := by omega
              simp [hlt, heq, hgt]
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then c i else 0) +
          (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val = k.val then c i else 0) +
          (∑ i : Fin n, if k.val < i.val then c i else 0) := by
          simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_assoc]
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then c i else 0) +
          c k +
          (∑ i : Fin n, if k.val < i.val then c i else 0) := by
          rw [sum_if_fin_val_eq k.val c]
          simp [k.isLt]

[Rank sum split at a cut]
  
  
  
  The rank sum is the weighted sum strictly left of \(k\), plus the
  contribution of \(k\), plus the weighted sum strictly right of \(k\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Use the same left/equal/right partition as for totals, now with each
  coordinate multiplied by its one-based rank.  The middle singleton sum
  is \((k+1)c_k\).

private lemma rankSum_split_at {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n) (c : Counts n) :
    rankSum c =
      leftRankSum k c + (k.val + 1) * c k + rightRankSum k c := by
  unfold rankSum leftRankSum rightRankSum
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n, (i.val + 1) * c i)
        = ∑ i : Fin n,
            ((if i.val < k.val then (i.val + 1) * c i else 0) +
              (if i.val = k.val then (i.val + 1) * c i else 0) +
              (if k.val < i.val then (i.val + 1) * c i else 0)) := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i hi
          by_cases hlt : i.val < k.val
          · have hne : i.val ≠ k.val := by omega
            have hnotgt : ¬ k.val < i.val := by omega
            simp [hlt, hne, hnotgt]
          · by_cases heq : i.val = k.val
            · simp [heq]
            · have hgt : k.val < i.val := by omega
              simp [hlt, heq, hgt]
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then (i.val + 1) * c i else 0) +
          (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val = k.val then (i.val + 1) * c i else 0) +
          (∑ i : Fin n, if k.val < i.val then (i.val + 1) * c i else 0) := by
          simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_assoc]
    _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then (i.val + 1) * c i else 0) +
          (k.val + 1) * c k +
          (∑ i : Fin n, if k.val < i.val then (i.val + 1) * c i else 0) := by
          rw [sum_if_fin_val_eq k.val (fun i : Fin n => (i.val + 1) * c i)]
          simp [k.isLt]

[Meldable total is divisible by three]
  
  
  
  The total multiplicity of any meldable vector is congruent to
  \(0\pmod3\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  In a meldable decomposition, triplets contribute multiples of \(3\).
  Each run contributes three tiles by
  Lemma~\ref{lem:red_run_count_sum}.  Summing these divisible
  contributions gives total residue \(0\).
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma meldable_total_mod {n : ℕ} (d : Counts n) (hd : Meldable d) :
    Nat.ModEq 3 (total d) 0 := by
  rcases hd with ⟨triplets, runs, hd⟩
  unfold total
  have hrewrite :
      (∑ i : Fin n, d i) =
        (∑ i : Fin n, 3 * triplets i) +
          (∑ j : Fin (n - 2), 3 * runs j) := by
    calc
      (∑ i : Fin n, d i)
          = ∑ i : Fin n,
              (3 * triplets i +
                ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                  if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) := by
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro i hi
              rw [hd i]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, 3 * triplets i) +
            ∑ i : Fin n,
              (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) := by
              simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, 3 * triplets i) +
            ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
              ∑ i : Fin n,
                if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0 := by
              rw [Finset.sum_comm]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, 3 * triplets i) +
            ∑ j : Fin (n - 2), 3 * runs j := by
              congr 1
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro j hj
              exact run_count_sum runs j
  rw [hrewrite]
  have hTriplets : Nat.ModEq 3 (∑ i : Fin n, 3 * triplets i) 0 := by
    apply sum_modEq_zero
    intro i
    apply Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd.mpr
    exact ⟨triplets i, by ring⟩
  have hRuns : Nat.ModEq 3 (∑ j : Fin (n - 2), 3 * runs j) 0 := by
    apply sum_modEq_zero
    intro j
    apply Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd.mpr
    exact ⟨runs j, by ring⟩
  simpa using Nat.ModEq.add hTriplets hRuns

[A run crossing a zero coordinate has zero count]
  
  
  
  In a meldable coordinate equation, if coordinate \(k\) has value \(0\),
  then every run whose support contains \(k\) has multiplicity \(0\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  At coordinate \(k\), the triplet contribution and all covering run
  contributions are natural numbers summing to \(0\).  Hence each
  covering run term is \(0\).

private lemma run_eq_zero_of_zero_coord {n : ℕ} {d : Counts n} {k : Fin n}
    {triplets : Counts n} {runs : Fin (n - 2) → ℕ}
    (hcoord : ∀ i : Fin n,
      d i =
        3 * triplets i +
          ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
            if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
    (hk0 : d k = 0) {j : Fin (n - 2)}
    (hcover : j.val ≤ k.val ∧ k.val ≤ j.val + 2) :
    runs j = 0 := by
  have hkcoord := hcoord k
  have hsum0 :
      (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
        if j.val ≤ k.val ∧ k.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) = 0 := by
    omega
  have hterm := eq_zero_of_sum_eq_zero hsum0 j
  simpa [hcover] using hterm

[Left total contribution of one run across a zero cut]
  
  
  
  If every run crossing a cut \(k\) has multiplicity \(0\), then the
  contribution of any single run to the total strictly left of \(k\) is
  congruent to \(0\pmod3\).
nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  A run wholly left of the cut contributes all three of its tiles; a run
  crossing the cut contributes \(0\) by hypothesis; a run wholly right of
  the cut contributes nothing to the left side.  Each case has residue
  \(0\).
nodes.lean_source:
private lemma run_left_count_mod {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n)
    (runs : Fin (n - 2) → ℕ)
    (hzeroCross : ∀ j : Fin (n - 2),
      j.val ≤ k.val ∧ k.val ≤ j.val + 2 → runs j = 0)
    (j : Fin (n - 2)) :
    Nat.ModEq 3
      (∑ i : Fin n,
        if i.val < k.val then
          (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
        else 0)
      0 := by
  by_cases hleft : j.val + 2 < k.val
  · have h_eq :
        (∑ i : Fin n,
          if i.val < k.val then
            (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
          else 0) =
          (∑ i : Fin n,
            if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i hi
      by_cases hcover : j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2
      · have hi_left : i.val < k.val := by omega
        simp [hcover, hi_left]
      · simp [hcover]
    rw [h_eq, run_count_sum]
    apply Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd.mpr
    exact ⟨runs j, by ring⟩
  · by_cases hcross : j.val ≤ k.val ∧ k.val ≤ j.val + 2
    · have hruns : runs j = 0 := hzeroCross j hcross
      simp [hruns]
      rfl
    · have hright : k.val < j.val := by omega
      have hzero :
          (∑ i : Fin n,
            if i.val < k.val then
              (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
            else 0) = 0 := by
        apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
        intro i hi
        by_cases hi_left : i.val < k.val
        · have hnot : ¬ (j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2) := by omega
          simp [hi_left, hnot]
        · simp [hi_left]
      rw [hzero]

        simp [hcover, hi_left]

  rcases hd with ⟨triplets, runs, hcoord⟩

      j.val ≤ k.val ∧ k.val ≤ j.val + 2 → runs j = 0 := by
    intro j hcover
    exact run_eq_zero_of_zero_coord hcoord hk0 hcover
  unfold leftTotal
  have hrewrite :
      (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then d i else 0) =
        (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then 3 * triplets i else 0) +
          (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
            ∑ i : Fin n,
              if i.val < k.val then
                (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
              else 0) := by
    calc
      (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then d i else 0)
          = ∑ i : Fin n,
              if i.val < k.val then
                (3 * triplets i +
                  ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                    if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
              else 0 := by
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro i hi
              rw [hcoord i]
      _ = ∑ i : Fin n,
            ((if i.val < k.val then 3 * triplets i else 0) +
              (if i.val < k.val then
                (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                  if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
              else 0)) := by
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro i hi
              by_cases hleft : i.val < k.val <;> simp [hleft]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then 3 * triplets i else 0) +
            ∑ i : Fin n,
              if i.val < k.val then
                (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                  if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
              else 0 := by
              simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then 3 * triplets i else 0) +
            ∑ i : Fin n,
              ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                if i.val < k.val then
                  (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
                else 0 := by
              congr 1
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro i hi
              by_cases hleft : i.val < k.val <;> simp [hleft]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then 3 * triplets i else 0) +
            ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
              ∑ i : Fin n,
                if i.val < k.val then
                  (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
                else 0 := by
              rw [Finset.sum_comm]

      Nat.ModEq 3 (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then 3 * triplets i else 0) 0 := by
    apply sum_modEq_zero
    intro i
    by_cases hleft : i.val < k.val
    · simp [hleft]
      apply Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd.mpr
      exact ⟨triplets i, by ring⟩
    · simp [hleft]

  have hRuns :
      Nat.ModEq 3
        (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
          ∑ i : Fin n,
            if i.val < k.val then
              (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)

      (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then (i.val + 1) * d i else 0) =

          (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
            ∑ i : Fin n,
              if i.val < k.val then
                (i.val + 1) *
                  (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
              else 0) := by
    calc
      (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then (i.val + 1) * d i else 0)

              if i.val < k.val then
                (i.val + 1) *
                  (3 * triplets i +
                    ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                      if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
              else 0 := by
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro i hi
              rw [hcoord i]
      _ = ∑ i : Fin n,
            ((if i.val < k.val then (i.val + 1) * (3 * triplets i) else 0) +
              (if i.val < k.val then
                (i.val + 1) *
                  (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                    if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
              else 0)) := by
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro i hi
              by_cases hleft : i.val < k.val <;> simp [hleft, Nat.mul_add]
      _ = (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then (i.val + 1) * (3 * triplets i) else 0) +
            ∑ i : Fin n,
              if i.val < k.val then
                (i.val + 1) *
                  (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                    if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)

              simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib]

            ∑ i : Fin n,
              ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
                if i.val < k.val then
                  (i.val + 1) *
                    (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)
                else 0 := by
              congr 1
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro i hi
              by_cases hleft : i.val < k.val <;> simp [hleft, Finset.mul_sum]

            ∑ j : Fin (n - 2),
              ∑ i : Fin n,
                if i.val < k.val then
                  (i.val + 1) *
                    (if j.val ≤ i.val ∧ i.val ≤ j.val + 2 then runs j else 0)

              rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  rw [hrewrite]

      Nat.ModEq 3
        (∑ i : Fin n, if i.val < k.val then (i.val + 1) * (3 * triplets i) else 0)

    by_cases hleft : i.val < k.val
    · simp [hleft]
      apply Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd.mpr
      exact ⟨(i.val + 1) * triplets i, by ring⟩
    · simp [hleft]
      rfl
  have hRuns :
      Nat.ModEq 3
        (∑ j : Fin (n - 2),

nodes.proof_tex:
\leanok
  Split the whole total into left, middle, and right parts.  The whole
  total and left total are both \(0\) modulo \(3\), and the middle value

nodes.lean_source:
private lemma meldable_rightTotal_mod_of_zero {n : ℕ} (d : Counts n) (k : Fin n)
    (hd : Meldable d) (hk0 : d k = 0) :
    Nat.ModEq 3 (rightTotal k d) 0 := by
  have htotal := meldable_total_mod d hd
  have hleft := meldable_leftTotal_mod_of_zero d k hd hk0
  have hsplit := total_split_at k d
